difference.reason: Both engines call the same paradl.postproc.checksum.ChecksumEngine.verify (Python hashlib); checksum cost is engine-independent, so no per-engine difference exists to measure.

checksum_large_file.note: 256 MiB crosses the 100 MiB mmap threshold in ChecksumEngine; this measures the real large-file path. Warm OS page-cache may lower the number -- it is not a WAN or engine-specific throughput claim.

aria2.note: Worker peak excludes the aria2c daemon child. Child peak (largest single reaped child) is reported separately and is NOT additive to the worker peak, so total aria2 footprint is understated; do not treat this as an apples-to-apples RSS win.

aria2.reason: Not measured: a faithful aria2 recycle comparison requires a live aria2c daemon with an active GID on a throttled URI (pause/unpause + changeUri); calling control RPCs on a nonexistent GID returns instantly and would understate real control-plane cost. The diagnosis doc records ~150 ms for this path, but it is not reproduced here, so the value is null by design.

engine_pinning.method: aria2 runs pin get_active_engine()='aria2', spy on Aria2Engine._use_rust_for, and sentinel RustEngine.download to fail on silent fallback (+assert a real aria2c daemon spawned). Native runs pin 'rust' and assert no aria2 daemon. --self-test-pin proves both the positive and the deliberately-broken case.

codeload.reason: No codeload/WAN comparison performed: this harness intentionally uses an isolated loopback server for reproducible CPU/socket measurement, so no accelerated URL is involved. If a codeload comparison is added, both engines MUST use the SAME accelerated URL -- otherwise the result is not an engine comparison.

honesty.drift: The ~1.2-1.3x cross-run drift documented in PARALLEL_DL_DEV_CONTEXT.md sec.7 is measurement noise, NOT a code-attributable win. See variance.
honesty.unfair_metrics: Metrics that cannot be measured fairly are written as {'value': null, 'reason': '...'} and never invented.
honesty.warm_cache: Warm throughput includes daemon/socket reuse + page-cache hits and is NOT presented as a general speedup; cold-vs-cold is the engine comparison.
